decisions.rationale: X-linked amelogenesis imperfecta is a specific, uncategorized disease entity (the XAI form) named in the title, so it is annotated as a Specific Disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease); §5 minimum necessary span

decisions.rationale: 'abnormality' is a very general term used as an apposition head noun and is excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §4 (general terms such as abnormality)

decisions.rationale: Repeated full-name mention of X-linked amelogenesis imperfecta in the abstract body; duplicate mentions are each annotated.
The abbreviation XAI is the synonymous short form of the disease named in the preceding long form, so it is a separate Specific Disease mention.
XAI is used as the name of the disease in 'Three families with XAI', referring to one specific disease.
XAI is used as the name of the specific disease in 'linkage was established between XAI and several markers'.
XAI functions as a noun modifier of 'disease process', so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than a standalone head disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: 'disease' is a very general term that is excluded when it is not part of a specific disease name.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate §4 (general terms such as disease)

decisions.rationale: AIH1 appears in a parenthetical as an alternative designation for the XAI disease process, so it is treated as a synonymous disease mention.
AIH1 is used consistently as the name of the disease under study (its locus is being mapped), so this repeated disease designation is annotated as a duplicate mention.
Repeated use of AIH1 as the name of the disease under study ('AIH1 lies in the interval'), annotated as a duplicate disease mention.
AIH1 is used again as the designation of the disease in the locus-heterogeneity context, so it is annotated consistently as a disease mention.
XAI is used as the name of the disease in 'locus heterogeneity in XAI', referring to one specific disease.
